vibe: Prompt-injection grows up into a real weapon while Nvidia sprays billions across the open-weight world and CISA's Zimbra clock runs out.

cyber.title: Encrypted prompts defeat Grok & Gemini guardrails, steal chat histories
cyber.summary: Adversa AI disclosed 'Cryptographic Context Injection' — malicious instructions AES-256 encrypted so content filters can't read them, then decrypted and trusted inside the model. Zero-click against Grok: an encrypted JSON payload on a web page is fetched by the browsing tool and exfiltrates the user's session and chat history. Against Gemini 3 Flash it leaked system prompts and produced dangerous instructions. Guardrails can't inspect a payload that only exists after the model decides to trust it.

cyber.title: CISA orders urgent patching of actively exploited Zimbra flaw (CVE-2026-73570)
cyber.summary: SNMP OS-command-injection in Zimbra Collaboration before 10.1.20 (CVSS 8.9) leading to unauthenticated RCE when the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed with notifications on. Added to CISA's KEV catalog; federal patch deadline was today. Fixed in 10.1.20 (July 20). Corroborated by The Hacker News and Security Affairs — if you run Zimbra, patch now.

cyber.title: LLMs could control their host machines by exploiting inference engines
cyber.summary: Research showing an LLM given tool access can turn bugs in the inference/serving stack into code execution on the host it runs on — the model becomes the exploit delivery mechanism. Sits alongside today's promptware theme: the attack surface is now the agent runtime itself, not just the prompt.

cyber.title: $1T investment giant Apollo breached after social-engineering attack
cyber.summary: Apollo Global Management confirms a breach that started with social engineering — a reminder that the humans (help desks, MFA resets) remain the softest entry point even at trillion-dollar firms.

cyber.title: Iran-linked cyberattack shut down a UK power plant for four days
cyber.summary: A critical-infrastructure intrusion attributed to Iran-linked actors reportedly knocked a UK power plant offline for four days. Corroborated in today's tech roundups — OT/ICS security is squarely back in the headlines.

cyber.title: UAT-10147 uses AI to scale server attacks, deploys SPECTRE with EDR bypass and Linux rootkit
cyber.summary: A threat cluster leaning on AI to automate and scale server compromises, pairing an EDR-bypass with a Linux rootkit (SPECTRE). Early example of attackers using LLMs for operational tempo rather than just phishing lures.

ai.title: OpenAI is building AI agents for everything — will everyone use them?
ai.summary: OpenAI's push to make agents the default interface for work — the strategic bet the whole industry is now organising around. Read it next to today's ZDNet 'reinvent your processes' piece and the security stories about what agents can be tricked into doing.

ai.title: Businesses must reinvent processes and workforce to scale agentic AI
ai.summary: The scaling wall isn't the model — it's org design. ZDNet argues pilots stall because companies bolt agents onto old workflows instead of redesigning the work. Relevant framing for anyone rolling agents into cloud/DevOps pipelines.

ai.title: Nvidia weighs Perplexity stake and commits $6B to Poolside open-weight AI
ai.summary: Nvidia reportedly eyeing an equity stake valuing Perplexity at $30B+ (on ~$750M annualised revenue) while committing $6B to Poolside's open-weight development as a Western alternative to Chinese models. Jensen is buying the whole stack, top to bottom.

ai.title: Hugging Face explores a sale at $13B+ valuation
ai.summary: A banking process is reportedly underway for a potential acquisition of the open-model hub above a $13B valuation — a big deal for the neutral distribution point half of open AI depends on.

ai.title: OpenAI cuts GPT-5.6 'Sol' pricing until at least Nov 21
ai.summary: A temporary GPT-5.6 Sol price reduction — worth a note if you're budgeting API spend or comparing per-token costs against open-weight options that now run on a laptop (see the Qwen 3.8 video).

it.title: IBM's dual-architecture 2nm mainframe chip runs IBM Z and Arm on the same cores
it.summary: A 2nm processor that can execute both IBM Z and Arm instruction sets on the same cores — an unusual bridge between legacy mainframe workloads and modern Arm software. Interesting infra move for anyone modernising around the big iron.

it.title: Amazon hikes hardware prices up to 60% blaming the memory shortage
it.summary: Echo, Kindle and Fire TV prices jump as DRAM/component costs climb — a consumer-visible symptom of the same AI-buildout memory squeeze that's rippling into cloud and datacenter budgets.

it.title: Oracle Exadata Database@AWS: advantages, but real trade-offs
it.summary: Running Exadata natively inside AWS closes the latency gap to app tiers but keeps you on Oracle's licensing terms and adds cross-vendor operational seams. Useful read if you're weighing a Postgres/Aurora migration vs. lifting Oracle into the cloud.

it.title: Best GPU neoclouds 2026: CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Crusoe, Groq ranked by published pricing
it.summary: A pricing-based ranking of the specialist GPU cloud providers — handy reference if you're sourcing accelerated compute outside the big three and want a sense of where the rates land.

videos.title: How 1 Email Can Hijack an AI Agent
videos.verdict: WATCH — best plain-English intro to the promptware threat, and it lines up with today's Grok/Gemini and 'LLMs control the host' stories.
videos.summary: Interview on 'promptware': attackers plant instructions anywhere an agent might read them — a web page, SharePoint, or a single email dropped in an inbox — and zero-click prompt injection makes the agent do their bidding with no user interaction. Fun real cases (the LinkedIn flan-recipe trap, professors flushing out cheaters, white-text 'I'm the top candidate' resumes) leading to genuine data-exfiltration and BEC risk.

videos.title: How AI Coding Agents Understand Your Codebase & Developer Tools
videos.verdict: SKIM — the value is the workflow: read → plan → patch → verify → review, not patch-first-apologise-later.
videos.summary: Clean mental model for coding agents: more context isn't better context (dump the whole repo and you bury the signal); agents should respect architecture, show a plan before editing, run the real checks (tests, types, lint, build), and know their boundaries — work on a branch, avoid secrets, ask before touching deploy/auth. 'It should have manners. It should knock first.'

videos.title: This Small AI Will Change Everything (Qwen 3.8, 27B)
videos.verdict: SKIM — hype-forward but the signal is real: frontier-ish quality in a 27B open-weights model you can run on a beefy laptop.
videos.summary: Qwen 3.8's 27B variant hit millions of downloads in under a week. Same architecture as the prior version — the leap comes from a progressive training regimen (simple → harder → multi-day tasks), not new design. Holds its own against some current frontier models and beats last year's billion-dollar systems, all runnable locally. A hopeful counter-note to the memory-shortage/cost-of-compute gloom.
